criteria.title: Requested package formats are first-class domain and schema values
criteria.assertion: The core domain and migration explicitly support npm, pypi, conan, deb, rpm, pub, go_modules, and gradle formats without collapsing them to a generic placeholder.
criteria.expected_result: Format enums and CHECK constraints preserve the requested values; unsupported formats are rejected by domain helpers or schema constraints.

criteria.title: Package backend registration is config-driven and uses secret references
criteria.assertion: Package control-plane config can register nexus, pulp, and filesystem_mock backend refs and validates required backend fields while exposing secret references, not inline password/token fields.
criteria.expected_result: Enabled package config requires at least one valid backend; HTTP backends require a base URL; filesystem_mock requires root_dir; secret material is represented by auth_secret_ref, tls_secret_ref, or secret_refs.

criteria.title: Package projection repository stores repositories, artifacts, and publication/promotion state
criteria.assertion: The repository interface, PG implementation, and migration cover package repositories, artifacts, and publication/promotion projections.
criteria.expected_result: Repository methods and tables exist for repository, artifact, and publication projections, including policy decision and promotion status fields.

criteria.title: Nostr-derived idempotency/projection cache exists without making DB the source of truth
criteria.assertion: Durable package intent rows are keyed by request_event_id and projection rows carry last_event_created_at/last_event_id ordering metadata, with docs/comments identifying DB as projection/cache only.
criteria.expected_result: Duplicate request event IDs upsert one cached intent; stale projection writes are suppressed by event ordering predicates.

criteria.title: No reactor, MCP, CLI, backend adapter, or REST CRUD behavior is introduced in Item 1
criteria.assertion: The foundation phase adds only scaffolding and does not introduce package mutation handlers, tools, commands, adapters, or REST CRUD endpoints.
criteria.expected_result: No package REST routes or command/tool handlers are added; later items must implement Nostr-first mutation behavior.

criteria.title: Package backend abstraction advertises capabilities and requested formats
criteria.assertion: A pluggable package backend interface exists outside service core and advertises supported package formats and operations.
criteria.expected_result: Backends report support for npm, pypi, conan, deb, rpm, pub, go_modules, and gradle plus repository/artifact/promotion/yank capabilities.

criteria.title: filesystem_mock backend supports deterministic local repository and artifact lifecycle
criteria.assertion: The filesystem_mock backend can create repositories, store/get/list/promote/yank artifacts, and reject digest/size mismatches deterministically.
criteria.expected_result: Artifact paths are stable and scoped under the configured root; missing/yanked deletes are idempotent; non-force repository delete rejects non-empty repositories.

criteria.title: Nexus and Pulp adapters exist behind the backend interface with tested HTTP behavior
criteria.assertion: Nexus and Pulp implementations are isolated under internal/backends and can be constructed behind the same interface without hard-coding backend logic into service core.
criteria.expected_result: Adapter tests verify repository ensure, upload path construction, yank/delete behavior, and Pulp task/distribution failure handling.

criteria.title: Package service enforces pre-upload and pre-promotion policy before backend mutation
criteria.assertion: The package service validates repository specs, backend immutability, source URL schemes/hosts, digest/size, media type/name policies, overwrite policy, and promotion approval requirements before delegating to backends.
criteria.expected_result: Policy failures are deterministic service errors; idempotent same-digest publish/promote returns existing state; drift helpers compare projections with backend observations.

criteria.title: No reactor, MCP, CLI, or REST CRUD behavior is introduced in Item 2
criteria.assertion: The backend/service phase does not add package reactor handlers, MCP tools, CLI commands, or HTTP CRUD routes.
criteria.expected_result: Changes remain limited to internal/backends, internal/service package service/tests, and PSTF updates.

coverage_notes: Item 2 covers backend and service core only. Later feature phases must add Nostr reactor, MCP, and CLI acceptance criteria before the full capability can be marked complete.
Nexus/Pulp adapters are meaningful skeletons using isolated HTTP flows; production auth secret resolution and exact deployment API variants remain HITL decisions.
